framework.name: EU AI Act
framework.description: EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation 2024/1689) — risk-based framework for AI systems. In force August 2024. High-risk AI providers must comply by August 2026.

objects.title: Risk Management
objects.description: Risk management system, identification, estimation, evaluation, and mitigation for high-risk AI systems.

objects.title: Data & Training
objects.description: Data governance, quality, bias detection, and special categories of data for AI training datasets.

objects.title: Transparency & Documentation
objects.description: Technical documentation, automatic logging, transparency to deployers, and information to affected persons.

objects.title: Human Oversight
objects.description: Human oversight design, override capability, output interpretation, and deployer oversight measures.

objects.title: Operational Requirements
objects.description: Accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity, post-market monitoring, incident reporting, and input data management.

objects.title: Governance & Market
objects.description: Quality management system, conformity assessment, EU declaration of conformity, EU AI database registration, and fundamental rights impact assessment.

objects.title: Risk Management System (Art. 9)
objects.description: A continuous, iterative risk management system is established, implemented, documented, and maintained throughout the high-risk AI system lifecycle.

objects.title: Risk Identification and Analysis (Art. 9(2))
objects.description: Known and foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system may pose to health, safety, or fundamental rights are identified and analysed.

objects.title: Risk Estimation and Evaluation (Art. 9(4))
objects.description: Risks arising from the use of the AI system in accordance with its intended purpose and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse are estimated and evaluated.

objects.title: Risk Mitigation Measures (Art. 9(6))
objects.description: Appropriate and targeted risk mitigation measures are adopted; residual risks are communicated to deployers and users.

objects.title: Data Governance (Art. 10)
objects.description: Training, validation, and testing datasets are subject to appropriate data governance and management practices covering design choices, data collection, labelling, and bias examination.

objects.title: Data Quality (Art. 10(3))
objects.description: Training, validation, and testing datasets are relevant, sufficiently representative, free of errors, and complete with respect to the intended purpose.

objects.title: Bias Detection and Mitigation (Art. 10(5))
objects.description: Datasets are examined for possible biases that could affect health, safety, or fundamental rights; appropriate mitigation measures are implemented.

objects.title: Special Categories of Data (Art. 10(6))
objects.description: Processing of special categories of personal data in datasets is necessary and proportionate, protected by appropriate safeguards, and documented.

objects.title: Technical Documentation (Art. 11)
objects.description: Technical documentation is drawn up before market placement and kept up to date throughout the lifecycle, enabling assessment of conformity (Annex IV).

objects.title: Automatic Logging (Art. 12)
objects.description: High-risk AI systems have logging capabilities ensuring traceability of system operation; logs are retained for the required period.

objects.title: Transparency to Deployers (Art. 13)
objects.description: High-risk AI systems are sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret outputs and use them appropriately; instructions for use are provided.

objects.title: Information to Affected Persons (Art. 50)
objects.description: Natural persons interacting with or subject to AI system decisions are informed in a clear and meaningful manner.

objects.title: Human Oversight Design (Art. 14)
objects.description: High-risk AI systems are designed and developed to allow effective human oversight, including the ability to intervene, stop, or override system decisions.

objects.title: Override Capability (Art. 14(4)(d))
objects.description: The AI system can be overridden or interrupted via a "stop" button or similar procedure; the system can be put in safe mode.

objects.title: Output Interpretation (Art. 14(4)(a))
objects.description: Deployers are enabled to fully understand the AI system's capacities and limitations and properly interpret its outputs.

objects.title: Deployer Oversight Measures (Art. 26)
objects.description: Deployers implement appropriate human oversight measures, assign competent persons, and monitor AI system operation with particular attention to risks.

objects.title: Accuracy, Robustness, Cybersecurity (Art. 15)
objects.description: High-risk AI systems achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, and are resilient with regard to errors, faults, inconsistencies, and adversarial attacks.

objects.title: Post-Market Monitoring (Art. 72)
objects.description: Providers establish a post-market monitoring plan and systematically collect and review data on system performance throughout the lifecycle.

objects.title: Incident Reporting (Art. 73)
objects.description: Serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems are reported to the competent national authority without undue delay (within 15 days for serious incidents).

objects.title: Input Data Management (Art. 26(5))
objects.description: Deployers ensure input data is relevant and sufficiently representative for the AI system's intended purpose.

objects.title: Quality Management System (Art. 17)
objects.description: Providers implement a quality management system ensuring compliance with this Regulation, covering strategy, design, development, testing, market surveillance, and documentation.

objects.title: Conformity Assessment (Art. 43)
objects.description: Before market placement, the AI system undergoes the appropriate conformity assessment procedure (self-assessment or third-party).

objects.title: EU Declaration of Conformity (Art. 47)
objects.description: A declaration of conformity is drawn up for each high-risk AI system and kept for 10 years after market placement.

objects.title: Registration in EU AI Database (Art. 49)
objects.description: High-risk AI systems are registered in the EU database before being placed on the market or put into service.

objects.title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (Art. 27)
objects.description: Deployers in public or regulated contexts conduct a fundamental rights impact assessment before deploying high-risk AI systems.
